title: Tiered security questionnaire fast-lane with SLA-backed credits and audit export
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem:
Enterprise deals are routinely delayed by lengthy security questionnaire cycles (SIG/CAIQ/SSP). Sales and solutions teams estimate 2–6 weeks of back-and-forth for mid-size customers; legal and security teams invest significant manual effort. Current attestation tooling is modular but unpriced in a way that enables predictable SLA-backed responses.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a paid "Fast Lane" for security questionnaire responses: a tiered, SLA-backed service that customers can purchase as credits (per-question or per-package) and/or as a short-term add-on to accelerate SIG/CAIQ turnarounds. Each purchase tier maps to a guaranteed response SLA (48h / 24h / 4h) and returns an auditable evidence package export (PDF + structured answers + optional cryptographic signature) suitable for enterprise contract handoff. The feature is surfaced in the Console Security Hub and available as an upsell during sales negotiations.

Key components and scope (MVP):
- Pricing model: per-question credits with bundled packages (50/200/600 credits) and three SLA multipliers; optional subscription add-on for monthly fast-lane credits.
- Console UX: Security Hub purchase flow, status tracker (queued / in progress / delivered), and audit export button.
- Response pipeline: internal responder queue + template engine using curated answer library and evidence attachments (logs, architecture diagrams, third-party attestations).
- Deliverable: Structured CAIQ/SSP export + rendered PDF + time-stamped audit trail. Optional cryptographic signing is out-of-scope for MVP (see stretch).
- Billing: integrate with usage billing to debit credits on acceptance; support invoice/contracted billing for enterprise customers.

Success metrics / hypothesis to validate:
- Time-to-first-deliverable for pilot customers reduced by >= 60% (target from median 14 days to <= 6 days).
- Deal acceleration: reduce sales cycle length for participating customers by >= 15%.
- Revenue signal: >= $Xk revenue per pilot month from fast-lane purchases (pricing experiment to determine X).
- CSAT for security responses >= 4.2/5 for pilot cohort.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Overpromising on SLA creates operational risk; need capacity guardrails and auto-throttles.
- Evidence quality: automated template answers may not be sufficient for complex customer variants; require manual review step for flagged questions.
- Legal/compliance sign-off required for any package labeled as an "attestation" — work with Legal to agree wording.
- Pricing complexity may confuse buyers; initial go-to-market should favor simple bundles and clear examples.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Discovery & scoping (2 weeks): capture top 15 commonly asked CAIQ modules, map answer templates, and estimate per-question effort.
2) Engineering spike (2 sprints): implement responder queue, status API, and export generator (PDF + JSON).
3) Console & Billing (1 sprint): UI flows for purchase and status; integration with billing to consume credits.
4) Pilot (4–6 weeks): run pilot with 5 customers (mix of SMB and mid-market) via Solutions/SE.
5) Iterate & scale (post-pilot): introduce auto-scaling responder pool, SLA throttles, and optional cryptographic signing.

Open decisions:
- Billing unit: per-question vs per-package vs hybrid (recommended hybrid for launch).
- SLA enforcement policy: soft SLA (best-effort with credits expensed back on miss) vs hard SLA (refunds/discounts). Recommended: start soft SLA and collect reliability data.
- Inclusion of custom questionnaire formats (outside CAIQ) in MVP. Recommend: MVP limited to standard CAIQ modules only.

Dependencies:
- Answer library and evidence pack templates (Research/Policies team).
- Billing platform changes to support one-off credit purchases and invoice consumption.
- Console components for purchasing and file-export flows.

Risks & mitigation:
- High demand could outstrip responder capacity: build auto-queueing and pre-sold capacity limits; offer estimated delivery time at purchase.
- Regulatory wording: Legal must review exported package language to avoid giving unintended guarantees.

Next steps (2-week cadence):
- Kickoff with Eng/Design/Legal on 2026-02-28.
- Pricing experiment design with Growth by 2026-03-08.
- Select pilot customers (Solutions) by 2026-03-15.
